# Unit test for function split_words
def test_split_words():
    # Case 1: Text with spaces -> split on whitespace
    assert split_words("hello world") == ["hello", "world"]
    assert split_words("one two three") == ["one", "two", "three"]

    # Case 2: Text with commas (no spaces) -> commas treated as separators
    assert split_words("hello,world") == ["hello", "world"]
    assert split_words("a,b,c") == ["a", "b", "c"]
    assert split_words("apple,banana,cherry") == ["apple", "banana", "cherry"]

    # Case 3: No spaces or commas -> count lowercase letters with even ord
    # 'b'=98, 'd'=100, 'f'=102, 'h'=104, 'j'=106, 'l'=108, 'n'=110,
    # 'p'=112, 'r'=114, 't'=116, 'v'=118, 'x'=120, 'z'=122 (all even)
    # 'a'=97, 'c'=99, 'e'=101, ... (all odd)
    assert split_words("abcde") == 2   # b, d
    assert split_words("abcdef") == 3  # b, d, f
    assert split_words("bdfhjlnprtvxz") == 13  # all even-ord lowercase letters
    assert split_words("xyz") == 2     # x(120), z(122); y(121) is odd
    assert split_words("") == 0        # empty string
    assert split_words("12345") == 0   # no lowercase letters
    assert split_words("HELLO") == 0   # no lowercase letters
    assert split_words("Hello World") == ["Hello", "World"]  # space takes priority
    assert split_words("a,b c") == ["a,b", "c"]  # space takes priority over comma

    print("All test_split_words tests passed!")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    test_split_words()
